[element-index-term]
=== `<index-term>` Index Term

An index term to be embedded into the narrative of a standards document so that an Index can be created programmatically.

#### Usage/Remarks
Index entries are recursive, so if a category (“drinks”) contains a sub-category (“lemonade”), the category <<element-index-term,`<index-term>`>> will contain two components: its own <<element-term,`<term>`>> (“drinks”), and an <<element-index-term,`<index-term>`>> for the sub-category. This subordinate index term will contain its own <<element-term,`<term>`>> (“lemonade”).
[source,xml]
....
<index-term>
 <term>drinks</term>
 <index-term>
  <term>lemonade</term>
 </index-term>
</index-term>
....
An <<element-index-term,`<index-term>`>> is either a single target point or the start of an index range. When it is the start of a range, an <<attribute-id,`@id`>> attribute is required, so that the <<element-index-term-range-end,`<index-term-range-end>`>> element can point to the start of the range.

#### Description

The following, in order: <<element-term,`<term>`>> <<element-term,Term>> Any one of: <<element-index-term,`<index-term>`>> <<element-index-term,Index Term>> Any combination of: <<element-see,`<see>`>> <<element-see,See (in an index term)>> <<element-see-also,`<see-also>`>> <<element-see-also,See-Also (in an index-term)>>
#### Content Model

[source,xml]
....
<!ELEMENT index-term    %index-term-model;                           >
....
#### Expanded Content Model

(term, (index-term | (see | see-also)*))
